blockers.finding: The public adapter identity and Python name-mangled secret/controller fields are recoverable from the same-process adapter object. An independent caller used only the adapter object plus an already-valid Kira profile to issue and stage a migration receipt.
blockers.impact: The claimed adapter-owned authorization boundary is not a security boundary inside the shared Python process. Promotion would let unrelated in-process code invoke a person-profile migration without a distinct protected authority service.

blockers.finding: The adapter verifies route-source bytes only during construction. After the verified Kira shell source was changed in an isolated clone, the existing adapter still issued and staged a Kira migration under the stale sealed source digest.
blockers.impact: A route can change after initialization while receipts and staged attachments continue to claim the old verified route bytes.

required_successor: Move issuance authority outside the inspectable shared Python object boundary or keep production integration disconnected.
Bind each issue and stage operation to a freshly rehashed exact route-source snapshot and reject any post-construction drift.
Add hostile regressions for same-process attribute introspection and route-source mutation after adapter construction.
Require another different fresh static audit before any promotion or rollout.
